title: A comparative clinical and audiological study of the transition from passive to active bone-conduction implants
summary:
In this study, we are investigating whether replacing the processor or even the Sophono implant can improve patients’ objective and subjective hearing performance, as well as their perceived quality of life. In the past, patients received this implant to compensate for a conductive hearing loss in the affected ear.
In the years since their implants were fitted, there have been many technical and medical advances, both in the implants and processors themselves and in their programming.
The aim is to demonstrate that newer implants, processors and coding strategies provide a measurable benefit for users of the aforementioned implant.
As part of the study, patients with the aforementioned implant will first undergo a series of hearing tests, on the basis of which a decision will be made, in consultation with the patient, as to whether there is an indication (i.e. the decision to proceed with treatment and its medical justification) for replacing the implant’s processor or the entire implant. Following the respective treatment, the hearing tests will be repeated to assess whether a significant improvement in hearing performance has been achieved as a result of the treatment, and to what extent.
conditions: Unilateral or bilateral conductive hearing loss, or mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss with previous implantatation of a Sophono-implant in one or both ears

interventions.name: Patients with conductive or mixed hearing loss who have previously been fitted with a so-called Sophono implant will be fitted with a new audioprocessor or bone conducting implant, depending on their hearing performance. The tests listed under ‘outcome’ will be carried out before and after the refit

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Unilateral or bilateral, relatively stable conductive hearing loss, or mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss
• Presence of a cochlear implant in one or both ears
• Bone conduction threshold of <45 dB and an average air-bone gap (4PTA) >20 dB
• Suitability for all examinations required for the study
• Signed and dated consent form
Exclusion criteria:
• Mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss (sensorineural threshold >45 dB)
• Retrocochlear or central hearing loss
• Known intolerance to the materials
• Skin conditions, particularly of the scalp, which prevent the wearing of the audioprocessor or interfere with its use
• Any physical, psychological or emotional condition that impedes the ability to undergo audiological examinations or to use the audio processor
